_note_wager_basis: how the results ledgers (the home page, scripts/pnl.py) count winnings and losses. 'entry': each entry is one wager; a winning entry's winnings are its payout over its own fee, a losing entry's loss is its fee (no netting between entries). 'fees': every payout is winnings and every entry fee a loss, so the loss cap also bites on the fees of winning entries; the conservative reading. Unsettled for DFS: ask a CPA. The home page shows the other count as its last row. The NFL after-tax backtest counts per entry (its spec).
_note_reporting_mode: business = the play is filed as a trade or business (Schedule C): losses and business_expenses (the year's data, subscriptions, server) come off the winnings without itemizing, capped at loss_cap_pct of them and at the winnings; the profit left carries self-employment tax (se_tax; ss_wage_base less w2_wages is the room left under the Social Security base). gross_165d = a hobby (losses only by itemizing). net_dfs = taxed on the profit.
_note: 2026 federal figures as understood in Oct 2026; VERIFY with a CPA before relying on them. brackets are [lower_bound, rate] rows per filing status. defaults.use_brackets switches the engine from the flat marginal_rate to the bracket table layered on other_taxable_income.
